title: Comparing Uncertainty Measurement and Mitigation Methods for LLMs
finding: Hallucination with confident wrong output is a leading, under-measured LLM failure; calibration degrades after post-training.

title: A Survey of Confidence Estimation and Calibration in Large Language Models
authors: Geng, Cai, Wang, Koeppl, Nakov & Gurevych
finding: Verbalized confidence collapses into overconfidence; models express certainty that does not track accuracy.

title: Large Legal Fictions: Profiling Legal Hallucinations in LLMs
finding: Hallucination of 69-88% on targeted legal queries, paired with systematic overconfidence in the fabrications.

title: Mind the Confidence Gap: Overconfidence, Calibration, Distractor Effects
finding: Large RLHF models hold calibration strengths yet can worsen on easy queries; effect varies by model size and question type.

title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can Beat Scaling Parameters
finding: Optimally allocating inference-time compute can beat scaling model parameters on accuracy.

title: Monte Carlo Tree Search Boosts Reasoning via Iterative Preference Learning
finding: AlphaZero-style look-ahead search over reasoning steps measurably improves correctness.

title: A Taxonomy of Test-Time Scaling for Reasoning (System-2 in LLMs)
finding: Across methods, trading inference compute for deliberation yields a distinct scaling law for reasoning quality.

title: Interpretable Contrastive Monte Carlo Tree Search Reasoning (SC-MCTS*)
finding: Tree search improves reasoning but its main drawback is slower speed; gains need careful reward-model design.

title: Deep Ensembles: A Loss Landscape Perspective
finding: Decorrelation from independent random initialization explores diverse modes and improves uncertainty and OOD robustness.

title: Pathologies of Predictive Diversity in Deep Ensembles
finding: Forcing predictive diversity hurts high-capacity deep ensembles; more accurate, less diverse members can win.

title: DICE: Diversity in Deep Ensembles via Conditional Redundancy
finding: Diversity helps only when explicitly traded against individual member accuracy; naive diversity drops performance.
